title: Best Investment Management Software for Distributions (2027)
summary: Real-estate syndication software that accelerates capital raising. We've already helped many real-estate syndicators raise $100MM+ using Cash Flow Portal.
body_markdown:
Distribution day is when mistakes show up. A wrong preferred return, a missed catch-up or a split applied to the wrong class lands in your investors’ bank accounts and inboxes, and fixing it means clawbacks and awkward emails.


The right software calculates the waterfall exactly as your operating agreement says, lets you check the numbers before anything goes out, pays investors and tells them what they received. This guide compares seven platforms on how well they do that: Cash Flow Portal, InvestNext, Agora, Juniper Square, AppFolio Investment Manager, Covercy and SponsorCloud.


If you’re still choosing a platform for the rest of your workflow, see our guides to the[best CRM for real estate investors and fund managers](https://www.cashflowportal.com/blog/best-crm-for-real-estate-investors-and-fund-managers-2027) ,[investment management software with fund admin services](https://www.cashflowportal.com/blog/best-investment-management-software-with-fund-admin-services-2027) and[investment management software for equity raising](https://www.cashflowportal.com/blog/best-investment-management-software-for-equity-raising-2027) .


*Disclosure: Cash Flow Portal publishes this guide and is one of the platforms compared. We use public information from each vendor’s website and public G2 ratings, and we point out where our own platform falls short.*


## How a distribution waterfall works


A distribution waterfall is the order in which a deal’s cash goes to limited partners (LPs) and the general partner (GP). Each tier fills before the next one starts.


Here’s a simple example. A deal distributes $1,000,000 after a sale. LPs put in $600,000 and have an 8% preferred return that has built up to $200,000. The GP gets a 30% share of profits with a full catch-up.


1. **Return of capital:** LPs get their $600,000 back.
2. **Preferred return:** LPs get their $200,000 pref.
3. **GP catch-up:** The GP gets $85,714, so it now holds 30% of profits paid so far.
4. **Split:** The remaining $114,286 is split 70/30. LPs get $80,000 and the GP gets $34,286.


In total, LPs receive $880,000 and the GP receives $120,000, which is 30% of the $400,000 profit. Real deals add more: several share classes, IRR hurdles, different prefs for different investors and side letters. That’s where spreadsheets break and software earns its keep. *(Illustrative only.)*


## What distribution software should include


- **Comprehensive waterfalls:** It handles every structure you use, including prefs, catch-ups, IRR hurdles, multiple classes and promote tiers, without workarounds.
- **Accuracy:** You can preview the numbers before paying, and every payment has an audit trail.
- **Ease of use:** Setting up a waterfall and running a distribution takes minutes, not a day of spreadsheet work.
- **Paying LPs:** It sends ACH or checks from the platform and handles IRA custodians and reinvestments.
- **What LPs see:** Investors get a clear notice, a statement in their portal and, at year end, their K-1.


## How we evaluated each platform


We asked five questions of each platform:


1. Can it run your exact waterfall on the plan you’d buy?
2. Can you preview a distribution and see an audit trail afterward?
3. Who runs the distribution: your team, or the vendor’s admin team?
4. How does it pay investors, including IRA custodians and LPs outside the US?
5. What do LPs receive: notices, statements and K-1s?


## Which platforms fit which firm size


We group firms by equity under management (EUM):


- **Emerging:** under $10M
- **Lower-middle:** $10M to $50M
- **Middle:** $50M to $200M
- **Upper-middle:** $200M to $1B
- **Institutional:** $1B and up

## 1. Cash Flow Portal


Cash Flow Portal is an investment management platform for real estate sponsors. Its Distribution Engine (trademark pending) models your waterfall from your legal documents and runs it on every plan.


**Strengths**


- Models waterfalls exactly as written in your operating agreement, including prefs, catch-ups, IRR hurdles, promote tiers and GP true-ups, with no tier upgrade needed.
- You set up and change waterfalls yourself, without waiting on a support team.
- Handles multiple share classes in one deal, such as a main LP class and a friends-and-family class, plus open-end funds, REITs and debt investments.
- Runs more than one waterfall per deal, such as one for the hold period and another for the sale.
- Calculates each LP’s accrued preferred return automatically every day, to the day or to the month.
- Supports equalization payments, so later investors can pay an entry fee on top of or inside their investment and earlier investors aren’t diluted.
- Lets LPs reinvest all or part of a distribution into their capital balance, if you allow it.
- You choose which metrics LPs see, so you can hide IRR while it’s misleadingly negative before a sale.
- Pays investors by next-day ACH or check from CFP’s built-in banking, and notifies IRA custodians of distributions to self-directed IRA investors.
- Runs unified distributions across co-GPs, and each co-GP gets its own branded portal.
- Delivers K-1s through US tax partners, with a tax center in the LP portal.
- CFP’s fund admin team can run distributions for you if you’d rather not do it in-house.


**Trade-offs**


- Built-in banking is US dollars only. Payouts in other currencies have to be sent outside the platform.
- No native mobile app for LPs; investors use the web portal.
- Built for the middle market, so very large institutional firms may want a more custom setup.


**Best for:** Middle-market sponsors ($50M to $200M EUM) who want complex waterfalls and payouts in one place, especially those raising with co-GPs.


## 2. InvestNext


InvestNext is an investment management platform for real estate and private equity sponsors, with distributions built into its core product.


**Strengths**


- Handles prefs, IRR hurdles, multi-class catch-ups and promote tiers on one plan.
- Sends ACH and checks from the platform, with no NACHA files to upload to your bank.
- Keeps an audit record of each distribution.


**Trade-offs**


- Setting up even a simple pref and split can take more steps than expected.
- Co-GPs aren’t first-class: they don’t get their own branded portals.


**Best for:** Middle-market sponsors who run their own distributions and don’t raise with co-GPs.


## 3. Agora


Agora is a real estate investment management platform with a strong focus on automating distributions and investor reporting.


**Strengths**


- Says it can model any waterfall, including side letters and class-based waterfalls.
- Sends distribution notices and statements to investors automatically.
- Supports cross-border payments for LPs outside the US.
- Pays by one-click ACH or generates NACHA files for your bank.


**Trade-offs**


- Some G2 reviewers mention a learning curve and a lot of setup at the start.
- Some G2 reviewers ask for more flexibility in promote structures.
- No native co-GP workflows.


**Best for:** Upper-middle firms ($200M to $1B EUM) with investors abroad who want automated notices.


## 4. Juniper Square


Juniper Square is an investment management platform for larger and institutional firms. Its Treasury Services team handles distributions for you.


**Strengths**


- Its admin team calculates allocations and generates distribution notices.
- Pays investors by check, wire or ACH, with approval workflows before money moves.
- Notices follow ILPA guidelines, which institutional LPs often expect.
- Capital activity statements are available in the investor portal.


**Trade-offs**


- Distributions are run by Juniper’s team rather than self-serve, so you have less hands-on control.
- Payments go out from your existing bank account rather than built-in banking.
- The most expensive option here ($$$$), with quote-only pricing.
- Some sponsors report that structures like a GP true-up aren’t supported natively.
- No separate accounts for co-sponsors.


**Best for:** Institutional firms ($1B+ EUM) that want an outside team to run distributions.


## 5. AppFolio Investment Manager


AppFolio Investment Manager is the investment side of AppFolio, best known for its property management software.


**Strengths**


- Includes a waterfall tool for complex funds, covering prefs, promotes and tiers, with audit reports.
- Pays investors by ACH or check.
- Lets you build custom investor reports.
- Connects to AppFolio’s property management data if you already use it.


**Trade-offs**


- We couldn’t find distribution notices documented on its public site.
- Some older G2 reviews ask for more waterfall options.
- No co-sponsor support.


**Best for:** Upper-middle firms that already run their properties on AppFolio.


## 6. Covercy


Covercy is an investment management and banking platform for real estate sponsors, with pricing aimed at smaller firms.


**Strengths**


- Handles prefs, catch-ups, promotes and IRR hurdles.
- Pays by ACH, wire, check or SWIFT, with multi-currency support.
- Sends personalized distribution notices.
- Includes approval steps and an audit trail.


**Trade-offs**


- Pricing is per entity, so costs add up as you add deals.
- Co-sponsor features aren’t documented on its public site.


**Best for:** Lower-middle firms ($10M to $50M EUM), especially those with investors outside the US.


## 7. SponsorCloud


SponsorCloud is a lower-cost investment management platform for newer sponsors.


**Strengths**


- Supports multi-tier waterfalls with prefs, catch-ups and splits.
- Pays by ACH or check, as one-time or recurring distributions.
- Sends branded distribution emails.
- Offers K-1s through tax service partners and IRA support through Equity Trust.


**Trade-offs**


- Co-sponsors work through the lead GP’s link rather than their own accounts.
- Some reviewers report slow support.
- Too few G2 reviews to give a reliable rating.


**Best for:** Emerging sponsors (under $10M EUM) running simple waterfalls on a tight budget.

### Questions to ask in a demo


- Can you run our exact waterfall live, using our operating agreement?
- Is that waterfall included in the plan we’d buy, or does it need an upgrade?
- Can we preview a distribution before money moves, and see an audit trail after?
- How do you handle IRA custodians, reinvestments and investors abroad?
- What will our investors see: the notice, the portal statement and the K-1?


## FAQ


### What is a distribution waterfall?


A distribution waterfall is the order in which a real estate deal’s cash goes to investors and the sponsor. Typically LPs get their capital back first, then a preferred return, then the GP catches up, and the rest is split by an agreed percentage.


### What is a preferred return?


A preferred return (pref) is the return LPs receive before the GP shares in profits, often 6% to 8% a year. If it isn’t paid in a given year, it usually builds up and is paid from later distributions.


### Should I pay investors by ACH or check?


ACH is faster, cheaper to process and easier to track, so most sponsors default to it. Checks are still useful for investors who ask for them or for some IRA custodians.


### Should I run distributions myself or use a fund administrator?


If your waterfalls are standard and your team is comfortable with the software, running them yourself is quicker and cheaper. If you have many entities, complex structures or limited staff, a fund admin team, such as Juniper Square’s or Cash Flow Portal’s, can take the work off your plate.
